incidents.victim: Three U.S. organizations (Michigan firm, Oregon tech company, Texas school)
incidents.vector: Network intrusions in 2019-2020 deploying Ryuk ransomware on hundreds of compromised servers and workstations, extorting Bitcoin for decryption keys.
incidents.impact: Armenian national Karen Vardanyan pleaded guilty to computer fraud and extortion conspiracy; he agreed to roughly $1.2M in restitution and faces up to 15 years. The Ryuk crew took in about 1,160 BTC (over $15M at the time).

incidents.victim: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor accidentally committed privileged Amazon AWS GovCloud access keys to a public GitHub repository, discovered by a security researcher in May.
incidents.impact: CISA's forensic report found none of the leaked credentials were used externally and no customer or mission data was exposed; the agency rotated all secrets and is adding repository monitoring after congressional scrutiny.

incidents.victim: Balochistan Police, Pakistan
incidents.vector: A China-linked operator compromised the Balochistan Police complaint-management system and planted malware disguised as a fake portal update, infecting both officers and citizens; a separate India-linked group ran a parallel campaign against the same force.
incidents.impact: Two unconnected state espionage operations (Feb 2024 - Apr 2026) exfiltrated internal-security data including criminal records, biometrics and personnel files, in some cases breaching the same systems.

incidents.victim: Enterprises worldwide (manufacturing most-targeted; 580 victims across 77 countries)
incidents.vector: A ransomware-as-a-service crew gains initial access via edge-device exploits (firewalls/VPNs), stolen credentials and access brokers, then uses a custom EDR-killer and self-propagating encryptors targeting VMware ESXi and virtual infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Now the second-most-active ransomware operation of 2026 by victim count, claiming 580 victims since inception and offering affiliates an unusually high 90% ransom cut to fuel rapid recruitment and growth.

incidents.victim: 142,000+ victims globally (individuals, businesses, governments)
incidents.vector: Social-engineering scam syndicates ran business email compromise, sextortion, romance scams, impersonation and investment fraud plus money laundering across 97 countries.
incidents.impact: Interpol's Operation First Light produced more than 5,800 arrests and $293M seized, identified 15,500+ suspects and blocked over 31,000 bank accounts; one Thai suspect alone processed more than $122.5M in 10 months.

incidents.victim: Five U.S. companies (nonprofit, financial services, hospitality and others)
incidents.vector: A rogue ransomware negotiator leaked clients' confidential negotiating positions and insurance limits to ransomware affiliates via backchannels to inflate ransoms, and separately deployed ransomware against additional companies.
incidents.impact: Angelo Martino III was sentenced to 70 months and had $10M in assets seized after helping extort a combined $75.3M from five victims he was hired to protect; two co-conspirators received four years each.

incidents.victim: Unidentified U.S. organization
incidents.vector: A ransomware-as-a-service crew ran a bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver attack, dropping a Microsoft-signed malicious kernel driver to kill endpoint security, plus AnyDesk, open-source credential stealers and PsExec for lateral movement before deploying its new locker.
incidents.impact: The attacker disabled security telemetry using a driver that carried a legitimate Microsoft Hardware Compatibility signature, entrenched in the victim network and deployed ransomware, highlighting the lag in Microsoft's vulnerable-driver blocklist.

incidents.victim: Website owners and small-to-medium businesses (global; many Australian SMBs hit)
incidents.vector: Mass scanning and exploitation of known CMS and plugin vulnerabilities (unauthenticated file upload, RCE, SSRF and deserialization flaws across WordPress, Craft, Joomla and others) to deploy webshells.
incidents.impact: Webshells give attackers remote control of web servers, enabling defacement, credential and data theft, malware distribution to visitors and pivoting into broader networks; ACSC issued a critical alert as many SMBs were already compromised.

incidents.victim: High-value targets reached via compromised Ruckus and ASUS edge routers
incidents.vector: A China-nexus actor exploits known vulnerabilities in unpatched Ruckus and ASUS routers to deploy custom backdoors and build a covert operational relay box (ORB) proxy network.
incidents.impact: The resilient, decentralized relay infrastructure lets other state-linked actors mask their origins and bypass perimeter defenses when attacking high-value targets; Cisco Talos published indicators to detect the malware suite.

incidents.victim: Odido (Dutch telecom provider)
incidents.vector: A Dutch-speaking man posing as an Odido IT employee used vishing to trick customer-service staff into granting access to a customer contact system, enabling bulk record downloads.
incidents.impact: Personal data of more than 6 million customers was exposed in the February 2026 attack; Dutch police took distribution servers offline and traced the intrusion to a suspected local accomplice.

incidents.victim: Undisclosed compromised organizations
incidents.vector: A modular Go backdoor combining a disk wiper, fake ransomware and a reused wiper module establishes persistence via a fake 'OneDrive Update' task and executes on-demand destructive commands.
incidents.impact: Microsoft observed environments being destructively wiped since October 2025; the malware overwrites raw disk content, removes partition metadata and encrypts files with keys that are never saved, rendering data unrecoverable.

incidents.victim: Windows / Microsoft Defender users (enterprise endpoints)
incidents.vector: A local elevation-of-privilege flaw in Windows Defender (CVE-2026-50656) escalates a standard user to SYSTEM; an anonymous researcher published a proof-of-concept exploit ahead of a patch amid a public feud with Microsoft.
incidents.impact: Microsoft issued an out-of-band patch; as a post-compromise tool the flaw lets attackers disable security telemetry, dump credentials and persist. In-the-wild exploitation is disputed but a public exploit is circulating.

incidents.victim: Unnamed organization (AWS cloud environment)
incidents.vector: An attacker brute-forced an internet-exposed AWS EC2 instance running an AI gateway connected to a foundation-model service, then deployed the XMRig cryptominer.
incidents.impact: Although used for cryptomining, the compromised AI gateway held broad access to foundation models, API keys, IAM roles and knowledge bases, illustrating how AI gateways create a high-value new attack surface.

incidents.victim: Transport for London, U.S. healthcare providers and multiple retailers
incidents.vector: Members of a native-English-speaking cybercrime collective used social engineering, phishing and SIM-swapping to steal employee credentials and MFA codes, then intruded into networks for extortion.
incidents.impact: Two members pleaded guilty in the UK to the 2024 Transport for London attack and hacking U.S. healthcare providers; one is also indicted in New Jersey over 120 intrusions at 47 U.S. entities linked to more than $115M in ransoms.

incidents.victim: 2M+ compromised consumer devices (smart TVs, streaming boxes)
incidents.vector: Proxy SDKs bundled inside TV-box and smart-TV apps silently conscripted devices into an always-on residential proxy botnet that was rented out to mask malicious traffic such as scraping, ad fraud and account takeover.
incidents.impact: The FBI and IRS-CI seized hundreds of NetNut/Popa domains and Google disabled command-and-control accounts and bundled apps, cutting the proxy pool by millions; the operating firm's stock fell about 67%.

incidents.victim: Israel (government and critical sectors)
incidents.vector: A broad surge of Iranian state-linked cyberattacks targeting Israeli government and critical-sector systems.
incidents.impact: Iranian attacks on Israel roughly tripled year over year, with Israel's National Cyber Directorate investigating about 4,800 incidents in June 2026 versus 1,600 in June 2025.

incidents.victim: Users of 119 malicious browser extensions (2.6M+ downloads)
incidents.vector: Malicious Edge, Chrome and Firefox extensions delivered genuine functionality but dropped payloads days after install, using steganography to hide commands while stealing credentials and committing affiliate fraud.
incidents.impact: Microsoft removed 119 malicious Edge add-ons downloaded by more than 2.6 million users; the long-running operation had ported its malware to the newer Manifest V3 standard despite its hardening.

incidents.victim: Latvijas Valsts Meži (LVM), Latvia's state-owned forestry company
incidents.vector: A foreign financially-motivated ransomware group exploited a vulnerability in a system that had not been updated for two years and dwelled for over a week before detection.
incidents.impact: The attack disrupted LVM's mapping platform, hunting app and contractor systems for weeks and leaked roughly 44 GB of stolen data; the company refuses to pay, and Latvia's election infrastructure was confirmed unaffected.

incidents.victim: Nidec Corporation (Japanese motor and electronics maker)
incidents.vector: A newly-launched ransomware operation breached Nidec's network and forced a full IT shutdown.
incidents.impact: The attackers demanded a $2M ransom and took the entire IT network offline; Nidec was also hit by ransomware in late 2024.

incidents.victim: ~20 technology and SaaS companies via a compromised vendor (Klue)
incidents.vector: Hackers breached vendor Klue, stole customer OAuth tokens and used them to reach downstream companies' Salesforce integrations and exfiltrate data.
incidents.impact: A cascading supply-chain data theft affecting roughly 20 downstream companies and growing, with sensitive Salesforce data stolen across the customer base.

incidents.victim: Tata Electronics (Apple supplier)
incidents.vector: A data-extortion group breached the supplier and, after its ransom was refused, leaked roughly 200,000 stolen documents.
incidents.impact: Leaked material included images of the unreleased iPhone 18 (battery, chips, circuit boards) and internal documents, exposing Apple supply-chain and product data.

incidents.victim: Central Bank of Libya
incidents.vector: A ransomware group breached the central bank's network and leaked stolen files on the dark web.
incidents.impact: Files allegedly taken from Libya's central bank were published by the attackers, and Libyan authorities opened an investigation.

incidents.victim: National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC)
incidents.vector: A cybercriminal group intruded into the U.S. insurance-standards body's network.
incidents.impact: The NAIC suspended risk designations for insurers and some credit-rating agencies paused data sharing to avoid exposure; the attackers were later evicted and operations are being restored.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Homeland Security — Homeland Security Information Network (HSIN)
incidents.vector: Intruders breached HSIN servers and a connected SharePoint system in late May to early June.
incidents.impact: The compromise hit a DHS network used to share sensitive information with federal, state, local and industry partners; the actor and the scope of stolen data remain unknown.
